target_customer: Customer experience and contact centre teams, including BPOs, that train and quality check support agents
problem: Manual QA reviews a tiny share of interactions and training is slow; Solidroad simulates conversations to train reps and scores live interactions.
product_category: AI training and quality assurance for customer experience teams

founders.name: Mark Hughes
previous_startups: Gradguide (exited late 2022; acquired by Native per Silicon Republic)

founders.name: Patrick Finlay
education: Trinity College Dublin, BAI Computer Engineering

technical_complexity.rationale: Realistic AI simulated customers, scoring across all channels and integrations with helpdesks require solid LLM engineering but rely on foundation models.

defensibility.rationale: Scorecards and enterprise integrations add some lock-in; roleplay training is copyable and crowded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Series A coverage names Medallia and Qualtrics as the established CX players; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: Contact centres review a small sample of conversations manually and BPOs need fast onboarding; Solidroad reports halving onboarding time at BPOs.

identity.logo: Icon and wordmark; design not described
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, practical and outcome focused; 'flight simulator for customer-facing teams'

brand_strength.rationale: Clean compound name and a vivid metaphor, but no mascot or community evidence.

pivots.from: Training simulations for sales and support reps
pivots.to: AI QA reviewing every customer interaction plus training
pivots.why: Series A framing; training remains in the product

outcome_analysis: Solidroad moved from a $1.2M angel round in July 2024 to a $6.5M seed led by First Round in June 2025 and a $25M Series A led by Hedosophia in April 2026. Named enterprise customers include Crypto.com, Ryanair and ActiveCampaign. Expansion from training into QA of all interactions drove the larger round.
notes: Seed of $6.5M seen in Built In, VentureBeat and Nordic9 snippets (not opened). Series A confirmed by the company post and several outlets. ZoomInfo's $64.7M total conflicts with all others and is ignored. Competitor sources found were dated 2025 or 2026, not near the Winter 2025 batch, so competitors left empty. No outcome events found beyond growth; founded year not found.
